messages.text: Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in Côte d'Ivoire changed by +13.8% per year (95% CI: +11.7% to +15.2%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is +5.3% relative to the previous 12 months.

messages.why: classification of 33 units, threshold ±1%/yr and p < 0.10
messages.text: Of 33 ADM2 units, 33 show significant growth, 0 are stagnating and 0 are declining. Light remains concentrated: District Autonome D'Abidjan accounts for 20% of national light.
Across ADM2 units, light per capita converges: the least-lit units are catching up.

The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is 2.23 in levels (95% CI: 1.73 to 2.73, R² = 0.96, 12 years) and −2.40 in growth rates (CI: −4.26 to −0.55). In pseudo-real time (each year predicted from earlier years only), light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of −0.49 (mean absolute error: 1.9 percentage points of growth, no better than the best naive forecast, error ratio 1.31).

messages.why: trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability
messages.text: The most pronounced shock in the seasonally adjusted series is “COVID-19”: trough of +20.0% (06/2020), return to the pre-shock level after 4 months.

messages.why: sensitive to the radiance threshold (from 0.00 to 4.26 M depending on the threshold); a proxy for outdoor lighting, not for grid connection
messages.text: The Gini coefficient of light per capita (ADM2) is 0.26 in 2025 (significant decrease since 2014). About 3.29 million people live in inhabited areas with no detectable light (11% of the inhabited population).

messages.why: 79% of zones confirmed by OpenStreetMap; candidates to be checked
messages.text: 24 candidate industrial zones are detected (2 major hubs, 4 energy sites), covering 65 km². They emit 3% of national light; the largest is District Autonome D'Abidjan (District Autonome D'Abidjan). Their light changes by +5.7% per year.

recommendations: Use night-time lights as a leading and subnational indicator, as a complement to — never a replacement for — the national accounts.
Publish regional GDP estimates as experimental statistics, with intervals and a methodological note, after comparison with available regional accounts.
Cross-check the map of populations “in the dark” against grid-connection registers: the average gap with the World Bank access rate is +11 percentage points.
Document breaks detected without an associated event (sensor change, outage, local event) before any economic interpretation.
Update the dashboard every quarter (monthly VIIRS series) and every year (annual VNL composites).

limits.title: What lights measure
limits.text: Upward radiance emitted around 01:30: agriculture, daytime trade, poorly lit services and the rural informal economy are poorly captured.

limits.title: Saturation and blooming
limits.text: DMSP saturates in city centres (DN 63) and “blooms” beyond lit areas; VIIRS is much better, but blooming still inflates the lit area of cities.

limits.title: Gas flares and isolated sites
limits.text: The automatic mask may remove isolated mines, ports or power plants, and miss small flares; candidates are exported for verification.

limits.title: Clouds, seasons, moon
limits.text: Cloudy months are only partially observed; STL removes average seasonality but not an abnormal season (snow, late monsoon).

limits.title: Product breaks
limits.text: DMSP and VIIRS are not directly comparable: the harmonised long series (Li et al., 2020) is a modelled product, to be read for trends only.

limits.title: NTL–GDP elasticity
limits.text: Estimated on 10 to 30 annual observations: wide intervals, possible instability, a non-causal relationship that varies with the level of development.

limits.title: Access to electricity
limits.text: “Inhabited without light” ≠ “not connected”: a connected household with low consumption is invisible; the indicator depends strongly on the radiance threshold and the population data.

limits.title: Administrative boundaries
limits.text: geoBoundaries/GAUL may differ from official boundaries; small ADM2 units are sensitive to light spilling over from neighbouring units.
